items.title: Ruth Brisbane interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013
items.q: Around the house she loved Bessie Smith

ctx.x: What kind of songs would she have sung around the house?

Around the house she loved Bessie Smith, and the heyday of her era was the Blues Era. She was born in 1900. So in the twenties she would have been in the twenties, a young woman. She was married and had children — a brood — with my dad. And she loved the blues. In fact, when I started singing she said you’ve got to learn a blues. I didn’t know a blues from, you know swing or whatever. I was listening to people like Ella and Dinah, and well Dinah was a good blues singer, but I couldn’t differentiate blues and…
That’s very interesting. I’ve read that some African-American households thought blues was the devil’s music, or something like that.
